Week1-Flowchart.title: CIA Triad: Cybersecurity Algorithm
Week1-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A doctor needs to access a patient's medical record. The doctor requests the record through the hospital's Access Control Panel. The system checks whether the doctor is authorized to see this record. If the doctor is not authorized, the request is denied and nothing more happens. If the doctor is authorized, the record is opened from the Patient Records Server and the access is written to the Audit Log System so there is always a record of who viewed what.

steps.title: Place Start>>1: Select Start and place it anywhere on the stage to begin your flowchart.
Add the Doctor>>1: Select Doctor and place it after Start.>>2: Connect Start → Doctor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>3: Add text: Request Patient Record

Check Authorization (Decision)>>1: Select Access Control Panel and place it after Doctor.>>2: Connect Doctor → Access Control Panel: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>3: Add text: Check Authorization>>4: Select Decision/Diamond and place it after Access Control Panel.>>5: Connect Access Control Panel → Decision/Diamond: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>6: Add text: Authorized?
If NOT Authorized>>1: Select Display/Screen and place it after the decision — this is the NO path.>>2: Connect NO → Display/Screen: Line Type: NO Connection Line>>3: Add text: Access Denied

If Authorized>>1: Select Patient Records Server and place it after the decision — this is the YES path.>>2: Connect YES → Patient Records Server: Line Type: YES Connection Line>>3: Add text: Open Patient Record

Log the Access>>1: Select Audit Log System and place it after Patient Records Server.>>2: Connect Patient Records Server → Audit Log System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>3: Add text: Record Access in Audit Log
Finish the Flowchart>>1: Select End and place it after Audit Log System.>>2: Connect all final results → End: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line

Week1-Flowchart.finalCheck: Start → Doctor → Access Control Panel → Authorized? → (Access Denied) or (Open Record → Audit Log) → End

Week2-Flowchart.title: User Authentication: Cybersecurity Algorithm
Week2-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user wants to log in on a computer. The user enters a username and password. The system checks whether these login details are correct. If the details are wrong, the login fails and the process stops. If the details are correct, the system scans the user's fingerprint to confirm their identity before finally granting access.

If Login is WRONG>>1: Select Display/Screen and place it after the decision — this is the NO path.>>2: Connect NO → Display/Screen: Line Type: NO Connection Line>>3: Add text: Login Failed

If Login is CORRECT>>1: Select Fingerprint Scanner and place it after the decision — this is the YES path.>>2: Connect YES → Fingerprint Scanner: Line Type: YES Connection Line>>3: Add text: Scan Fingerprint
Grant Access>>1: Select Display/Screen and place it after Fingerprint Scanner.>>2: Connect Fingerprint Scanner → Display/Screen: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>3: Add text: Access Granted
Finish the Flowchart>>1: Select End and place it after the final results.>>2: Connect all final results → End: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line

Week2-Flowchart.finalCheck: Start → User → Computer → Login Correct? → (Login Failed) or (Scan Fingerprint → Access Granted) → End

Week3-Flowchart.title: Phishing Email: Cybersecurity Decision Algorithm
Week3-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user receives an email asking them to click a link and confirm their account details. The message feels urgent and may be a phishing attempt. Before clicking anything, the user checks the sender's address and the link. If the email looks suspicious, the user must not click the link and should report it. If the email looks safe, the user can continue and visit the official website directly instead of clicking the link.

Week4-Flowchart.title: Weak Passwords: Cybersecurity Decision Algorithm
Week4-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user creates a password for a new account on a computer. The system checks whether the password is strong enough. If the password is weak, the user must create a stronger one before continuing. If the password is strong, it is stored securely and the account is protected.

Week5-Flowchart.title: Pretexting: Cybersecurity Decision Algorithm
Week5-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user gets a phone call from someone claiming to be an authorized person, asking for confidential information. Before sharing anything, the user must verify the caller's identity using a trusted method. If the identity cannot be verified, the user should not share any information and should report the call. If the identity is verified, the user may share only the information that is truly needed.

If Verified>>1: Select Process/Step and place it after the decision — this is the YES path.>>2: Connect YES → Process/Step: Line Type: YES Connection Line>>3: Add text: Share Only Required Information
Finish the Flowchart>>1: Select End and place it after the final results.>>2: Connect all final results → End: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line

Week5-Flowchart.finalCheck: Start → User → Phone Call → Identity Verified? → (Report the Call) or (Share Only What's Needed) → End

Week6-Flowchart.title: Ransomware: Cybersecurity Response Algorithm
Week6-Flowchart.algorithmIntro: A user notices files cannot be opened and a ransom message appears on the computer. The system checks whether this looks like a ransomware attack. If it is not ransomware, normal security checks simply continue. If ransomware is suspected, the device is disconnected from the network, the security team is informed, and the system is safely restored from a clean backup.

If NOT Ransomware>>1: Select Display/Screen and place it after the decision — this is the NO path.>>2: Connect NO → Display/Screen: Line Type: NO Connection Line>>3: Add text: Continue Normal Security Checks

If Ransomware is Suspected>>1: Select Process/Step and place it after the decision — this is the YES path.>>2: Connect YES → Process/Step: Line Type: YES Connection Line>>3: Add text: Disconnect Device from Network
Report It>>1: Select Security Monitor and place it after Process/Step.>>2: Connect Process/Step → Security Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>3: Add text: Report Incident to Security Team
Recover Safely>>1: Select Backup Server and place it after Security Monitor.>>2: Connect Security Monitor → Backup Server: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>3: Add text: Restore from Clean Backup
Finish the Flowchart>>1: Select End and place it after the final results.>>2: Connect all final results → End: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line
